The odds ratio of BCG vaccination on COVID-19 severity is approximately **1.14** (95% CI: 0.83–1.56, $p = 0.432$) in the primary proportional odds ordinal logistic regression model evaluated across the full study cohort ($N = 1,000$), controlling for prior medical history count, patient interaction frequency, and the interaction between the adjustment covariates (`mh_count × patients_seen`). 

When modeling patient interaction frequency as a numeric score (1 to 3), the resulting odds ratio is virtually identical at **1.14** (95% CI: 0.83–1.57, $p = 0.420$). In models incorporating all two-way interaction terms, the main effect odds ratio of BCG vaccination is **1.10** (95% CI: 0.69–1.75, $p = 0.699$) with categorical patient interaction frequency, and **1.31** (95% CI: 0.55–3.12, $p = 0.537$) with numeric coding. Across all specifications and sensitivity cohorts, BCG vaccination showed no statistically significant effect on COVID-19 severity ($p > 0.30$).
